result.headline: Roll tracked its setpoint worse from t=5-15 s; the data shows a lag during hard maneuvers, not a clear fault.
result.explanation: Roll error grew only while the roll setpoint swung 45 to -7 to 43 deg. The response lag is about 0.97 s both there and after t=15 s, so a normal lag during a maneuver fits better than a failed part.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] followed its setpoint worse from t=5 to 15 s: typical |error| up to 16.355 deg against 6.234 over the whole recording
evidence.shows: The only sustained control degradation sits in the 5-15 s window.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] typical |error| by stretch: 0-5 s 1.616, 5-10 s 14.595, 10-15 s 16.355, 15-20 s 4.431, 20-25 s 4.974, 25-30 s 4.609 deg
evidence.shows: Error returns to a few degrees after 15 s without any recorded event.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=9.771 to 10.776 s (peak |error| 36.047 deg)
evidence.shows: Worst divergence, during the fast setpoint swing back up from -7 deg.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.778 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: The only event, 4 s before any departure. No voltage series is recorded, so it cannot be tied to the roll behaviour.

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs roll response, t=5-15 s
checked.result: Correlation 0.521 at zero lag, 0.932 at lag 0.965 s; typical difference 15.539 deg, worst 36.047 deg at t=10.369 s.
Best lag 0.965 s again, correlation 0.959; typical difference 4.617 deg.

checked.check: Actuator outputs vs roll setpoint, t=3-15 s
checked.result: ch[1], ch[3], ch[4] and ch[5] move smoothly with the roll setpoint swing (ch[4] 1430-1685 us). No stuck or saturated output; ch[0], ch[6] and ch[7] are constant. These are commands, not surface position.
Pitch left baseline first at 3.065 s, then the roll setpoint at 3.112 s. Roll response left baseline at 6.365 s. The baseline was only 3 s, so this is weak ordering.

checked.check: Airspeed and throttle around the roll reversal
checked.result: Airspeed fell from about 17.9 to 12.6 m/s between 6.8 and 9.2 s. Throttle rose from 14 to 41% between 7 and 10.8 s.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.airspeed at t=8.306 s: 16.034 -> 13.606 m/s (step -2.428, 29.4x its usual variation)
effects.why: Airspeed loss follows the roll reversal and the pitch changes; the throttle rise at 8.675 s is the response.

effects.quote: CHANGE propulsion.throttle at t=8.675 s: 17 -> 32 % (step 15, 7.5x its usual variation)
effects.why: The throttle increase follows the airspeed drop, so it looks like the controller reacting.

next_action.action: Pull gyro roll rate, roll-rate setpoint and battery voltage for t=3-15 s
next_action.why: Separates a normal maneuver lag from a weak roll actuator or sensor fault. Only the rate loop and power data can do that.
how: Export the raw log for the same flight, t=3-15 s

next_action.baseline: The 15-30 s stretch of this flight, where lag is 0.965 s and error about 4.6 deg.

outcomes.then: Close as no fault; flag the aggressive setpoint profile.
